newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures surge on buy-backs, cash bonds firm.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures surge on buy-backs, cash bonds firm.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply higher on Wednesday on short-covering.
Short-covering pressure was strong as a shift in the benchmark from the March to the June contract approached, traders said.
Some said there was speculation that a hedge fund, which had sold JGB futures in large lots earlier in the week, may have been covering its short positions on Wednesday.
The March ended at 126.40, up sharply from the previous day"s 126.09. Turnover was 41,778 contracts.
"On Monday a foreign trader apparently placed large-lot sell orders at around 126.35," a brokerage house trader said.
A number of sell orders, each worth about 50 billion yen, were placed by the foreign trader, the brokerage house trader said.
The same foreign trader may have been trying to cover the short positions on Wednesday, a trust bank trader said.
Buy orders came in on Wednesday near the same levels as the large-lot sell orders on Monday, the trust bank trader said.
The trader said there was speculation that a hedge fund was behind the trades.
JGBs ignored a rise in Tokyo share prices, as traders were more concerned with adjusting their positions, a trader for an agricultural financial institution said.
In the Tokyo stock market, the benchmark Nikkei 225 average rose 128.37 points or 0.69 percent to close at 18,599.12.
In morning trade, players said they were focusing on the renewed weakness of bank stocks.

Major bank stocks fell across the board on Wednesday morning after credit-rating agency Moody"s said on Tuesday it had placed its senior debt ratings for three Japanese long-term credit banks under review for a possible downgrade.
Market yields for the long-term credit banks" debentures city bank"s securities unit said.
The Industrial Bank of Japan"s February five-year debentures were traded at 1.655 percent on Wednesday, up from a sell quote of 1.64 percent on Tuesday.
The Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan"s February debentures were traded at 1.95 percent on Wednesday, up from a sell quote of 1.94 percent on Tuesday.
There were no bids or offers for Nippon Credit Bank"s February debentures on Wednesday.
Traders said cash JGBs were firm on Wednesday.
Investors were detected buying cash bonds in various zones
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.370 percent as of 0700 GMT, down from the previous day"s 2.395 percent.
--Masayuki Kitano, Tokyo Treasury Desk, +81-3-5473-3748
